mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Monday, November 23, 2026. Anthropic has introduced Claude Ship, a new suite of AI agents designed to automate the review, correction, and approval of code changes within software development workflows. This development is significant because while AI coding assistants have improved the speed at which code is generated, the human-led process of reviewing and approving that code has created a bottleneck. Claude Ship aims to address this by delegating approval authority to AI agents based on policies defined by development teams. The suite includes a general-purpose code reviewer, an agent called PR Steward that manages issues like merge conflicts or failing checks, and an approval agent that functions according to user-defined policies. Because the approval functionality is in beta, the company recommends that teams initially use it in an observe-only mode to maintain safety and oversight. This ensures that organizations can monitor how the agent makes decisions before fully trusting it with the power to push changes to production environments. In the infrastructure sector, OpenAI and Cisco have launched Shirudo, an open-source runtime tool designed to protect Linux systems from vulnerabilities without requiring system restarts. Shirudo utilizes eBPF—a Linux technology that enables small programs to run within the operating system—to identify and block suspicious activity. By deploying these eBPF-based shields, security teams can mitigate threats like the Java4Shell exploit while continuing to run their services, providing a stopgap measure while permanent software patches are developed. This is critical for businesses that cannot afford the downtime associated with traditional system restarts. The project also emphasizes a trusted deployment model, where shields are cryptographically signed and verified to ensure security integrity. By utilizing hardware-backed verification through a Trusted Platform Module, operators can maintain a reliable record of the protections currently loaded on their systems. The ethics of AI consciousness have returned to the public discourse following recent comments from philosopher Thomas Nagel. In an interview, Nagel, a recipient of the Berggruen Prize, dismissed the idea that AI models could develop consciousness, arguing that the information processing performed by silicon circuits is not equivalent to the physical, biological experience of a brain. His remarks challenge Anthropic’s internal stance, which considers AI sentience a potential risk factor that necessitates specific safety rules. While debates continue, observers noted that current interest in AI consciousness often focuses on models capable of sophisticated language, whereas non-linguistic models like image generators do not typically trigger similar speculation. This highlights a persistent tension between the philosophical requirement of lived experience and the growing sophistication of AI-driven linguistic interaction. In robotics, researchers have released RoboTrack, a new suite of data and benchmarks designed to improve how robots perceive and track objects in real-world environments. The developers noted that existing trackers often perform well on controlled laboratory benchmarks but struggle with real-world complexities like cluttered scenes, occlusions, and changing viewpoints. By utilizing a new synthetic training dataset called RoboTrack-15M, the team demonstrated improved performance for robots performing tasks such as pipette handling in laboratory settings. This development matters because robust point tracking is essential for robots to reliably manipulate objects in dynamic environments where standard visual cues might be obstructed by grippers or crowded workspaces. In the financial sector, the startup Supertake has raised $20 million in seed funding for a platform that allows users to translate natural language market predictions into automated investment portfolios. The company, which is currently in an early phase, works with brokerages like Coinbase and Robinhood to execute these portfolios. While the system uses frontier AI models to interpret user insights, the developers clarified that the platform is intended as an evolution of the traditional robo-advisor experience rather than a prediction market.
